findings.description: Critical: The plan correctly addresses the core issue of having no persistent storage for candidate work stubs between supervisor cycles, providing a tracked file store at openspec/supervise/candidates/.
findings.resolution: The design properly specifies byte-stable writes with sort_keys and trailing newlines, and separates lifecycle state from the file content.

findings.description: Critical: The separation of concerns between rubric scoring (model) and ranking (deterministic script) is well-designed, maintaining the host-assisted invariant while enabling interpretable rankings.
findings.resolution: The design correctly splits subjective scoring to the model and objective ranking to the script, with proper caching and validation mechanisms.

findings.description: Critical: The bounded evidence loading with security measures (2 KiB per artifact, 64 KiB per batch, symlink/URI rejection, sanitization) properly addresses security concerns with untrusted provenance data.
findings.resolution: The implementation correctly uses contained regular file reading only, with proper redaction and delimiters for untrusted data.

findings.description: Nit: The 20-candidate cap is well-justified for performance but could be mentioned explicitly in the performance section of non-functional requirements.
findings.resolution: Consider adding the 20-candidate limit as an explicit performance target in the non-functional requirements table.

findings.description: Optional: The dependency resolution logic for cross-roadmap dependencies is clearly specified but could benefit from additional test scenarios covering edge cases.
findings.resolution: Add explicit test scenarios for complex cross-roadmap dependency chains in the test plan.

findings.description: Critical: The schema definitions for rubric scores and digest are comprehensive and align with the described behavior, including proper validation of stub keys and factor justifications.
findings.resolution: The JSON schemas properly enforce all constraints mentioned in the design document.

findings.description: FYI: The timeout and retry mechanism for rubric scoring (120 seconds, one retry) provides good resilience against model failures while preventing indefinite blocking.
findings.resolution: The timeout and retry settings are appropriate for maintaining system responsiveness.

findings.description: Critical: The dry-run behavior is properly specified to not write anything under openspec/supervise/, maintaining compatibility with existing workflows.
findings.resolution: The design correctly specifies that cached scores may be read but rebuilds are only emitted to stdout during dry-run.

findings.description: Optional: Consider adding more explicit observability metrics for tracking digest generation performance and rubric scoring success rates.
findings.resolution: Add specific metrics to track in the observability section of non-functional requirements.

findings.description: Critical: The work package decomposition is well-structured with clear dependencies and appropriate scope boundaries, enabling parallel implementation.
findings.resolution: The work package DAG properly sequences contract definition before implementation and separates concerns appropriately.
